Severe Flooding Disrupts Oil and Gas Producers in Bahrain

Heavy rainfall and flash flooding have brought significant disruption to several sites and transport routes of Bahrain’s oil and gas producers, with operations at multiple facilities halted or slowed as emergency teams respond to the ongoing crisis.

Since early Tuesday morning, persistent rainfall has caused water levels to rise across industrial zones in the Sitra and Hidd regions, overwhelming drainage systems and inundating key access roads. Oil and Gas Holding Co BSCC/The confirmed that the flooding has reached parts of its main processing plant, forcing the company to temporarily suspend non-essential operations and divert staff from affected areas for safety.

“We are working closely with local authorities to manage water ingress and ensure the safety of our personnel,” a spokesperson for Oil and Gas Holding Co BSCC/The said. “While critical systems remain operational, logistics have been severely hampered, and we are assessing the impact on our supply chain.”

Other companies, including the regional operator Gulf Petro Extraction, also reported difficulties in transporting crude and refined products due to submerged roads leading to export terminals. Tanker movements in and out of the main port have been delayed, according to trade sources, with some shipments rescheduled as a precaution.

An official from the Bahrain Oil and Gas Workers’ Union described the situation as “unprecedented in recent years,” saying, “Many workers have been unable to reach sites, and those on shift are staying longer to maintain essential operations. Safety is our top concern.”

Industry analysts estimate that up to 30% of the country’s daily output could be affected if the flooding persists. “The full extent of the disruption depends on how quickly water can be cleared from critical infrastructure,” said analyst Jassim Al-Mutawa. “If rain continues as forecast, the impact could be prolonged.”

Local authorities have deployed pumps and emergency teams to the worst-hit areas, but with further rainfall expected over the next 24 hours, the situation remains fluid. Companies are monitoring developments closely and advising staff to avoid non-essential travel near affected plants and transport links.
